Join us in this role where you’ll be responsible for sourcing the right suppliers to secure the operation and fulfil the servicing needs of our offshore windfarms. You’ll be working with our procurement process and governance from developing the sourcing strategies to contract handover. In this role, you'll be coordinating with our category managers, business stakeholders and colleagues in supporting functions. You can look forward to a dynamic, fast-paced, and international environment, where you’ll have the opportunity to develop your career while making your mark on the transition to renewable energy.

**Welcome to Offshore Generation Procurement

**You’ll be part of the Offshore Services Procurement team where you, together with your colleagues, will support our offshore windfarms to produce power, by ensuring contracting of timely, compliant and competitive O&M services capacity. You’ll be working in a global team of highly skilled procurement professionals. An important aspect of your role is to proactively consolidate input from internal stakeholders to negotiate and sign fit to scope contracts ready for the end users’ purposes. In this role you’ll be working closely with colleagues organized in projects at our operational hubs.

As a team, we ‘re driven by an open working environment where everyone is encouraged to speak up, seek, and provide feedback. We actively take initiative, work on improvements, and seek learning opportunities.

**You’ll play an important role in:

**

• being responsible for the end to end tendering process, qualifying suppliers, clarifying and evaluating bids, preparing and negotiating terms and conditions, and recommending and awarding suppliers

• ensuring compliance with internal and external tendering rules, policies, and governance by actively engaging and seeking input from key support functions

• preparing and presenting clear and thought-through gate documents to aim management and budget owners’ decision on recommended strategies

• leading communication with suppliers throughout the sourcing activities

• contributing to the quality assurance processes by reviewing peers’ documentation, sharing tendering and contract lessons learned, and providing feedback to category strategies

• handing over complete signed contract package with complete metadata ready for execution .

**To succeed in the role, you:

**

• have significant experience with managing sourcing processes from drafting of sourcing strategies to contract signing. Experience running tenders according to EU-tender law is a plus

• have a passion for negotiating and possess considerable experience taking responsibility for planning and executing negotiation process

• possess good verbal and written English communication skills enabling you to effectively collaborate with the team and communicate professionally with key stakeholders

• have the bandwidth to spot commercial opportunities focusing on bottom-line impact and personnel safety, while achieving the right technical, operational contract solution

• act with high integrity, take ownership, handles pressure well, proactively asks questions, and seeks input beyond your network to drive results

• are organized, well-structured, and possess good attention to detail, especially when preparing documentation.

Maybe you’ve read the above and can see you have some transferable skills, even though they don’t quite match all the points. If you think you can bring something to the team, we still encourage you to apply.

**Shape the future with us

**Send your application to us as soon as possible. We’ll be conducting interviews on a continuous basis and reserve the right to take down the advert when we’ve found the right candidate.

As an applicant or employee, you may request reasonable work and position accommodation or adjustments via accommodation@orsted.com.

Please note that this is a fixed-term position with a duration time of months.

Please note that for your application to be taken into consideration, you must submit your application via our online career pages and answer the screening questions relevant for your country. We don't take applications or inquiries from external recruiters or agencies into account for this position.

**Position salary range:

**For this position, the expected base pay range is kr55,680.00- kr69,600.00 for the advertised location. The offered base salary will be determined within this range based on relevant skills, experience, and expected role fulfilment within the stated pay range to ensure a fair and competitive offer. Where applicable, you may also be eligible for variable payment and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Our benefits package:

**For this position, employees who meet eligibility requirements have access to: employer‑paid pension (11% contribution), full insurance coverage (accident, life, critical illness, and health insurance); five weeks of paid holiday plus 10 additional paid days off per holiday year; a 3% holiday allowance; access to Ørsted Life & Fitness Vitality including fitness classes, physiotherapy, massage, and wellbeing programmes; a multimedia package (mobile phone, PC, internet); staff club membership with sport and cultural activities; and access to the company canteen (monthly lunch scheme or daily tickets).

**Pre-employment background check:

**Certain positions may require a background check as part of the hiring process. If applicable, you will be informed during the recruitment process. Background checks are conducted by an external provider in accordance with local legal requirements.

jobs.occupation: Service Manager Level 1 SCADA & Power Plant Control
jobs.description:
Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Job Description

Are you an experienced SCADA engineer or technical service lead who wants to remain hands-on while taking responsibility for reliable service delivery? Would you like to combine solving technical problems with guiding colleagues and improving business-critical services supporting renewable energy?

As our new Service Manager Level 1 SCADA & Power Plant Control, you will be responsible for the reliable, secure and efficient delivery of agreed SCADA and Power Plant Control services supporting Vattenfall’s renewable-energy operations. Your scope includes WTG and substation SCADA, hybrid park controllers and interfaces to WTG Power Plant Controllers.

You will combine hands-on SCADA engineering and incident resolution with functional leadership of a dedicated service team of Level 1 SCADA and Power Plant Control engineers. Alongside your own technical assignments, you will prioritise the team’s work, coordinate suppliers and support functions, and drive continual improvement while meeting agreed service levels.

Working closely with customers, stakeholders and the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, you will help develop standardised, proactive service delivery that combines effective incident response with preventive maintenance, lifecycle planning and long-term service improvement.

Be in your element with BA Wind

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets.

You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

Qualifications

Y****our role

You will take responsibility for the delivery and performance of the services within your agreed scope, from their introduction into operation through ongoing support, improvement and eventual replacement or retirement.

Your service scope covers Level 1 SCADA for WTGs and substations, together with assigned Power Plant Control systems and interfaces, including hybrid park controllers and interfaces to WTG Power Plant Controllers. You will take responsibility for their operational support, controlled changes, lifecycle management and continual improvement within agreed ownership boundaries.

This role combines hands-on senior SCADA engineering with functional service leadership and does not include personnel line management. You will personally undertake engineering work while coordinating and prioritising the service team’s activities, monitoring outcomes and making risks, dependencies and resource needs visible. Capability and capacity requirements will be aligned with the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, with resources requested from the respective line managers.

You will apply your practical engineering expertise to diagnose faults, restore services and implement controlled technical changes within your agreed scope and authorisation. You will provide technical guidance to colleagues, assess operational risks and challenge proposed solutions, combining hands-on delivery with effective planning and coordination across organisational boundaries.

You will participate in the team’s on-call rotation, personally diagnosing and resolving incidents affecting SCADA and Power Plant Control services outside normal working hours, within your agreed technical scope and authorisation. You will involve other engineers, OEMs and suppliers when specialist support is required, follow agreed escalation arrangements and contribute to root-cause investigations and corrective and preventive actions.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Service scope and support arrangements: Maintaining clear service definitions, ownership boundaries, agreed service levels, support responsibilities and escalation arrangements, aligned with the agreed service mapping, the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager and customer expectations.

• Service delivery and hands-on engineering: Managing reliable, secure and efficient day-to-day delivery of SCADA and Power Plant Control services, including monitoring, incidents, service requests, problems, changes and lifecycle activities. Personally configuring, testing, commissioning, maintaining and improving assigned systems, controllers and interfaces within approved procedures and authorisations, while balancing engineering assignments with service-leadership responsibilities and agreed priorities.

• Service performance: Monitoring performance against agreed service-level agreements (SLAs), key performance indicators (KPIs) and operational targets. Reporting on service availability, incident response and restoration, recurring issues, risks and improvement actions.

• Incident response and problem management: Personally diagnosing and resolving incidents affecting assigned SCADA systems, Power Plant Control systems and interfaces, while coordinating additional engineers, OEMs, suppliers and support functions as required. Ensuring timely service restoration and clear stakeholder updates, investigating root causes and implementing or assigning corrective and preventive actions, with follow-up to completion.

• Backlog and delivery planning: Managing and prioritising the service team’s backlog, dependencies and delivery plans based on higher-level guidance, operational impact, risk and available capacity. Planning your own engineering assignments alongside service-leadership responsibilities, balancing urgent operational needs with planned maintenance, lifecycle work and improvements, and making capacity trade-offs visible.

• Capability and capacity planning: Identifying the skills and capacity required to deliver agreed services and roadmap commitments, aligning them with the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager, and requesting resources from the respective line managers and making the consequences of resource gaps visible.

• Lifecycle engineering and controlled change: Executing the agreed service roadmap through hands-on engineering and coordination of upgrades, migrations, patching, configuration changes and lifecycle replacements. Preparing, implementing or reviewing assigned changes, with appropriate risk assessment, testing, rollback arrangements, documentation and operational handover through approved processes.

• Supplier and stakeholder coordination: Coordinating contributions from suppliers, specialists and internal support functions, monitoring delivery against agreed responsibilities and service commitments, and following up on issues. Supporting technical and service-related purchasing or contract discussions with the responsible procurement and contract owners.

• Project requirements and transition to operations: Providing OT operations and maintenance requirements to projects whose deliverables will enter the service team’s scope. Agreeing operational acceptance criteria with the relevant stakeholders and participating in readiness reviews and handovers, checking support coverage, monitoring, documentation, recovery arrangements and unresolved risks.

• Operational documentation and knowledge: Producing and maintaining technical records, configuration information, operational runbooks and troubleshooting guidance for your own engineering work. Ensuring that the service team maintains relevant service and asset records, clear support responsibilities, escalation arrangements and accessible operational knowledge.

• Continual improvement and technical guidance: Using service-performance data and operational experience to identify, prioritise and implement improvements that reduce recurring incidents and strengthen reliability, efficiency and supportability. Standardising repeatable services and work packages, contributing to technical reviews, and supporting colleagues through practical guidance, knowledge sharing and appropriate automation.

• Security, compliance and audit support: Ensuring that applicable cybersecurity, regulatory and operational requirements are incorporated into service delivery and lifecycle planning, in collaboration with the responsible service engineers, cybersecurity and compliance functions. Coordinating relevant evidence and follow-up actions for audits and reviews.

• Risk management and escalation: Maintaining visibility of service risks, dependencies, delivery constraints and outstanding decisions. Escalating issues beyond the service team’s mandate or capacity to the Asset Service Area OT O&M Manager and other responsible stakeholders, with clear recommendations and operational consequences.

Your profile / who are you?

You hold a relevant bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, automation or control engineering, computer engineering, industrial IT, systems engineering or a related discipline. Alternatively, you have developed equivalent professional competence through a relevant technical qualification and substantial hands-on experience in SCADA or industrial OT engineering and operational support.

You have several years of hands-on experience engineering, operating and supporting SCADA systems or comparable industrial OT solutions, including recent practical experience diagnosing faults, restoring services and implementing controlled changes. You can personally diagnose faults, restore services and implement controlled technical changes. You have also demonstrated the ability to coordinate technical work, prioritise operational needs and guide colleagues or suppliers. Your background may be as a senior engineer, technical lead or service manager who has remained technically active; a previous formal Service Manager title is not required.

You understand the demands of supporting business-critical systems and can translate operational needs into clear priorities, responsibilities and delivery plans. You are comfortable taking responsibility for service outcomes while working with engineers, suppliers and line managers in a matrix organisation.

You have excellent written and spoken English skills and can communicate effectively with both technical and non-technical stakeholders. The role may be subject to security clearance, and candidates must be able to meet the applicable screening requirements.

You bring knowledge and experience in:

• Operational service management: Applying structured incident, problem, service-request, change, configuration and lifecycle-management practices, with clear ownership, service levels and follow-up.

• Hands-on SCADA engineering: Practical experience configuring, integrating, testing, commissioning, maintaining, operating and supporting SCADA systems and interfaces, including documenting and validating technical changes.

• SCADA and OT environments: Understanding the role of SCADA in asset monitoring and control, including interfaces and dependencies between WTG and substation systems, power plant control, central control systems and supporting infrastructure. You can engage meaningfully with specialists and assess the operational implications of technical proposals.

• Service leadership and prioritisation: Coordinating multidisciplinary service teams and suppliers, managing backlogs and dependencies, identifying capacity requirements and resolving competing priorities within an agreed mandate.

• Operational resilience and secure engineering: Practical experience supporting service availability through monitoring, backup and recovery of SCADA applications and configurations, secure access, vulnerability handling and controlled technical changes, in collaboration with the teams responsible for supporting infrastructure.

• Service introduction and handover: Translating operations and maintenance needs into project requirements and acceptance criteria, assessing operational readiness and coordinating the transition of new or changed solutions into supported services.

• Supplier and stakeholder management: Establishing clear expectations, following up on service commitments, coordinating across organisational boundaries and handling escalations constructively.

• Incident and problem management: Diagnosing faults across SCADA applications, Power Plant Control systems, interfaces and connected systems, including dependencies on server services, networks, certificates and service accounts. Personally restoring services within your technical scope and authorisation, investigating root causes and implementing corrective and preventive actions, with specialist or supplier support where required.

• Performance analysis and improvement: Using service metrics, incident trends, risks and operational feedback to identify improvement priorities, track actions and communicate progress and results.

Additional experience that would be valuable:

• Experience with wind-turbine and substation SCADA platforms, hybrid park controllers, or OEM-specific WTG Power Plant Controllers and their interfaces.

• ITIL or comparable service-management training, or relevant OT cybersecurity training.

• Experience with service-management, backlog-planning, reporting and knowledge-management tools.

Personal traits

To succeed in this role, we believe that you:

• Take ownership of service outcomes and follow through on commitments, decisions and improvement actions.

• Lead through clear priorities, constructive challenge and collaboration, including where you do not have direct line authority.

• Remain calm and decisive during operational incidents, communicating clearly and involving the right people at the right time.

• Work in a structured and transparent way, making risks, dependencies, resource constraints and delivery progress visible.

• Use sound judgement to balance immediate service restoration, operational risk, long-term reliability, maintainability and agreed delivery priorities.

• Build effective relationships across engineering, Operations, projects, suppliers and support functions, and actively encourage knowledge sharing.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Location: Kolding, Denmark or Amsterdam, Netherlands

Additional Information

Our offer

Looking for a career with growth?

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

The scale and ambition of our wind, battery and solar business means you can

At Intempus, our goal is simple: make time tracking as easy, intelligent and automated as it can possibly be. We're building the future of time tracking and our ambitions are high. This means that our system needs to deliver a stable and great user experience at all times — especially since our user base keeps growing fast.

That’s why we're looking for you: an experienced DevOps Engineer ready for the challenge.

What we offer

• 
A role where you can grow, learn and make a real impact

• 
A helpful, social and diverse workplace with a flat hierarchy and open communication

• 
A healthy work/life balance

• 
55 friendly, driven and skilled colleagues

• 
Flexibility, including two days of remote work per week

• 
A centrally located, modern office at Visma House in Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen

• 
… and much more!

Your role

As part of our four people DevOps team, your main responsibility will be keeping our systems running smoothly around the clock. More specifically, you will:

• 
Develop and maintain CI/CD pipelines that ensure fast, reliable and secure delivery of changes to our applications

• 
Automate infrastructure and server configuration using tools like Ansible, Terraform or whatever fits best — we're moving from a fully manual setup to infrastructure and configuration that's fully documented and managed as code

• 
Monitor and troubleshoot day-to-day issues across our servers and applications

• 
Design and implement improvements using the best tools the DevOps ecosystem has to offer — anything from a new secrets management solution to better container deployment workflows

• 
Collaborate with developers to improve tooling around development and test environments

• 
Keep our infrastructure and applications updated and secure

• 
Automate wherever possible, to cut down on manual effort and maintenance overhead

Who are you?

You're proactive and take ownership of your work. You thrive in a team with plenty of freedom, where ideas are shared openly and people genuinely listen to and support each other.

You communicate clearly, both in writing and in person, and you actively help foster a good team environment.

You hold a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or equivalent, and you bring at least 7 years of experience in a DevOps role or similar (e.g. System Administrator).

On the technical side, you have experience with:

• 
Managing Linux systems for at least two years (we run Debian-based Linux across all our servers)

• 
Bash scripting — you're comfortable working in a bash shell

• 
Docker — building, testing, deploying and maintaining containerized applications in production

• 
A programming language (our CI/CD pipeline and much of our automation is written in Python)

• 
git

A CI/CD tool (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, etc.)

• 
An infrastructure-as-code tool, ideally Terraform

• 
A configuration management tool, ideally Ansible

• 
Container orchestration (e.g. Kubernetes, HashiCorp Nomad)

Nice to have, but not required:

• 
Managing PostgreSQL databases

• 
Cloud services with any provider

Who are we?

Intempus is a Danish software company with offices in Copenhagen and Aarhus. Since 2012, we've built, refined and optimized our own time-tracking system, and we continue to hold high ambitions for our product.

Our team of 55 includes a development team of 35 driven engineers. We are part of the Visma Group but operate day-to-day as an independent company.

Take a look at our team in the Copenhagen office here!

Ready to join us?

Apply now if you can see yourself as our new DevOps Engineer. Job start is January 1st, 2027, but we are flexible for the right candidate. The role is on-site at our office at Visma House in Carlsberg Byen, Copenhagen.

Please submit your application in English, as we are an international team, and include your resumé, educational diploma and references.

We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.description:

**Hilti Denmark is looking for a Digital & Strategy Marketing Manager to lead and develop our digital marketing, branding, communications, and strategic marketing initiatives. In this role, you will be responsible for driving an integrated marketing strategy that strengthens our brand, engages customers and employees, supports commercial growth, and delivers measurable business impact.

As part of the Danish Marketing Leadership Team, you will lead a team of five employees and collaborate closely with stakeholders across Sales, Marketing, Finance, and regional and global teams. This is a unique opportunity for an experienced marketing professional who enjoys combining strategic leadership with hands-on execution.

**What You'll Do

**As our Digital & Strategy Marketing Manager, you will be responsible for translating business priorities into impactful marketing initiatives while ensuring strong execution across digital channels, communications, campaigns, pricing, and strategic business projects.

**Your Responsibilities Will Include

**

• Lead and develop a high-performing marketing team, fostering a culture of collaboration, innovation, and accountability.

• Shape and execute Hilti Denmark's brand, communications, and digital marketing strategy to strengthen market position and customer engagement.

• Own the digital customer journey across content, social media, Hilti Online, and demand generation, driving traffic, conversion, and growth.

• Translate strategic business priorities into impactful go-to-market initiatives and integrated marketing campaigns.

• Use data, customer insights, and market intelligence to optimize performance and influence key business decisions.

• Partner across sales, finance, product, and trade functions to enhance commercial effectiveness, pricing excellence, and sustainable growth.

**What You’ll Bring

**We're looking for an ambitious marketing leader who combines strategic thinking with strong commercial understanding and the ability to turn ideas into action.

**We Imagine That You Have

**

• A university degree in Marketing, Business, or a related field, combined with solid experience in digital marketing, campaign management, strategic marketing, or similar disciplines.

• At least 5 years of experience operating successfully in cross-functional, matrix organizations, with a proven ability to influence stakeholders across functions and organizational levels.

• Strong leadership capabilities with experience developing people, fostering collaboration, and driving high-performing teams.

• A data-driven and analytical mindset, with excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to translate insights into business actions and growth opportunities.

• Hands-on experience with digital marketing channels, customer engagement, content strategies, and performance measurement, coupled with strong communication and storytelling skills.

• Fluency in English. Danish and experience within B2B and/or the construction industry are considered strong advantages.

**This is an opportunity to take ownership of a broad and highly visible marketing leadership role with significant business impact. You will combine people leadership, strategic responsibility, and operational execution while helping shape the future direction of Hilti Denmark's marketing organization.

• A leadership role with responsibility for key marketing activities and strategic business initiatives.

• The opportunity to lead and develop a talented team in a collaborative and high-performing environment.

• Close collaboration with senior leaders and international stakeholders across the Hilti organization.

• A dynamic role combining brand management, digital marketing, demand generation, analytics, and business strategy.

• Continuous development opportunities, supported by coaching, feedback, and extensive learning resources.

• Long-term career opportunities within a global organization known for developing its people.

**Hilti is a global leader in construction innovation, with more than 34,000 team members across 120 countries. Guided by our purpose, Making Construction Better, we’re driven to keep learning, growing, and finding new ways to make a lasting impact. Here, you’ll be empowered to use your strengths, work with a global and inclusive team, and take on meaningful challenges. At Hilti, you’ll have the chance to make your ideas, achievements, and growth real through purpose, passion, and teamwork.

**Commitment to Inclusion

**At Hilti, inclusion is a key focus in how we work, lead, and grow together. We are committed to embracing diversity of thought and creating an environment that is inclusive of everyone, everywhere. We continuously strive to ensure every voice is valued and every team member feels empowered to contribute. By building on this foundation, we strengthen our teams, our innovation, and our impact, making construction better together.

You can apply for this position by clicking “Apply now” and uploading your CV. You do not need to submit a cover letter, but we encourage you to include a few sentences in your CV about what motivates you to apply for the role.

If your profile matches the position, you will first be invited to a short video interview. After that, selected candidates will be invited for an in-person interview. If you have any questions about the position, you are very welcome to contact our recruitment team at DKTeamRecruiting@hilti.com

**Do you want to help ensure quality in energy infrastructure projects? Can you turn quality requirements into practical activities and support projects through to handover? And do you have experience with quality management, audits and inspections? Then join COWI as our new Quality Consultant.

****Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

**We are looking for a Quality Consultant to join COWI and support our customers’ construction and operational projects on assignments of both shorter and longer duration. You will help ensure that projects follow the customer’s governance framework and can be handed over to the operations organisation at the required quality level, with all supporting documentation. Your work may span electricity transmission projects, including cables, overhead lines and substations; gas distribution and transmission networks, including natural gas and biogas facilities and stations; oil pipelines; and gas storage facilities.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Support projects in applying internal processes and tools and provide guidance and support on quality-related matters.

• Consistently promote and embed quality management in projects so that documentation, products and deliverables meet the specified requirements

• Plan, carry out and document the necessary quality activities in collaboration with the project team, including internal and external audits and inspections of project partners.

• Ensure that quality-related experience and lessons learned are shared within the customer’s organisation.

• Prepare project quality plans.

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

**The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways, but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

You work in a structured and systematic way and take a proactive approach to building relationships. You collaborate and communicate on an equal footing with internal and external stakeholders involved in construction projects. You bring professional credibility in your field and can work independently.

On top of that, you will have:

• An understanding of the structure and application of quality management systems.

• Experience with project- and process-related work.

• Experience with quality management activities in infrastructure and construction projects, including quality assurance (QA) and providing input to quality control (QC) activities.

• Experience carrying out quality activities, including audits and inspections of internal and external parties involved in projects.

• Experience using the Microsoft Office suite.

• The ability to communicate in Danish and English, both orally and in writing, at negotiation level.

Your official COWI office location will be either Lyngby, Vejle or Aarhus. However, your primary workplace will be at Energinet in Erritsø, but Ballerup could also be an option, with some travel to Erritsø. You will report to Head of Discipline, Ioana Nicoleta Tuglui, who is based at COWI's headquarters in Lyngby.

**A place to work and so much more

**At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

**Before you apply

**All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key

**We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

Looking for a workplace where you can make real change? A meaningful job where you have the freedom, trust and responsibilities to play an important role and not just be a small fish in a big shoal? Does being a part of a social, passionate, and international team sound right to you? Join us!

Your position

In your new position as a Telecom & Network Engineer in the Telecom Engineering Department, you will join a multicultural, diverse team of skilled, enthusiastic telecommunication specialists from all over the world. “How fast can we ship this?” comes up a lot at Pandektes. So does “we should take our time with this one.”

**Knowing when it’s good enough

**We like getting things into customers’ hands quickly. That means making trade-offs, questioning scope, and accepting when something is good enough for now. There’s usually another approach to explore or another prompt to try. At some point, you have to ship.

We use AI throughout our development process. AI code reviews, feature flags, and remote coding agents running end-to-end tests help us move quickly with confidence. Deciding what to build, what to check, and when it’s ready still takes judgment.

**Knowing when to slow down

**Some decisions deserve more time. Getting them right makes everything that follows easier. Getting them wrong means paying for the same mistake repeatedly.

Our default is to move quickly, so slowing down takes discipline. Sometimes it means pushing back when the rest of us want to get something out. We value someone who can explain why the extra work matters, challenge an approach, and help us decide where to spend our time.
